summary: Recommends running integration tests in Docker or restricted environments, shows running all or specific targets with ansible-test integration, using -vvv or --retry-on-error, and notes ansible-test isn't getting new collection-testing features.
questions: How do I run integration tests for my collection in a container?
How do I run only one integration test target?
How can I get more verbose output when an integration test fails?
Which Docker image should I use for cloud module integration tests?
Is ansible-test still being actively developed for collections?

answer_card.title: Run collection integration tests
answer_card.answer_md:
Run in Docker since tests can install packages and start services:
```shell-session
ansible-test integration --docker fedora -v
ansible-test integration --docker fedora -v connection_bar
```
- Multiple target names are allowed (directory names under `tests/integration/targets/`).
- Use `-vvv`, or `--retry-on-error` to rerun failures more verbosely.
- Use the `default` image for platform-independent tests such as cloud modules.

`ansible-test` no longer gets feature enhancements for new collection testing needs; discussion is on the Ansible Forum (`collection-test-strat` tag).
